simple: This page shows how to make 3D models from a text description, like 'green dragon car with 4 wheels', using `GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync()`. Even players can do this while playing, and everyone in the server sees what was made. With a schema, the model comes out in separate pieces, like a body and four wheels, so it can actually work. Then 'retargetable scripts' add behavior so the car drives or the plane flies.
analogy: It is like ordering from a toy factory: you describe the toy (the prompt), pick a kit shape like 'car with 4 wheels' (the schema), and then snap in a ready-made motor (the retargetable script) that fits whatever car came out.
keyPoints: `GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync(inputs, schema)` creates a model from a text prompt.
The schema tells it how to split the model into parts. Right now there are two built-in ones: `Car5` (a body plus four wheels) and `Body1` (one single mesh).
Models made during the game are replicated, so every player sees them and can build together.
You can suggest a size and set a maximum triangle count to keep models fast to draw.
Generation can fail (for example, if the prompt is rejected or it takes too long), so wrap the call in `pcall`.
After generating, scale the model with `ScaleTo`, place it with `PivotTo`, and anchor its parts if it should stay still.
Retargetable scripts (from the `Behaviors.rbxm` file) adapt driving or flying behavior to whatever size and shape got generated.
With `Car5`, the parts have fixed names like `body` and `front left wheel`, so your script can find them.

terms.text prompt: The words you type to describe what to make, like 'purple bat car with 4 wheels'.
terms.schema: A plan that lists which separate parts to generate. `Car5` means five pieces: one body and four wheels.
terms.mesh / MeshPart: A 3D shape made of many tiny triangles. A `MeshPart` is a part that uses one.
terms.functional model: A model that does something, like a car you can drive, instead of just a statue.
terms.replicated: Copied from the server to every player's device so everyone sees it.
terms.fidelity: How detailed and accurate something looks.
terms.latency: The wait time before you get a result. Lower latency means faster.
terms.bounding box: An invisible box that fits around the whole model, used to suggest its size.
terms.triangle count: How many tiny triangles a mesh uses. Fewer triangles are faster to draw.
terms.pcall: A protected call. It runs a function and catches errors so your whole script does not crash.
terms.retargetable script: A script that adjusts itself to fit any generated model, like a car script that works whether the car is tiny or huge.
terms.behavior: The scripts, attachments, and constraints that make a model actually do things.

example.title: Generate a car from a prompt
example.code:
local GenerationService = game:GetService("GenerationService")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local inputs = {
	TextPrompt = "yellow sports car with a spoiler",
}
local schema = {
	PredefinedSchema = "Car5", -- body plus four wheels
}

-- Generation can fail, so use pcall to catch errors
local success, result = pcall(function()
	return GenerationService:GenerateModelAsync(inputs, schema)
end)

if success then
	-- Shrink or grow the model so its biggest side is 16 studs
	local size = result:GetExtentsSize()
	local scaleFactor = 16 / math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
	result:ScaleTo(scaleFactor)

	-- Anchor every part so the pieces do not fall apart
	for _, descendant in result:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			descendant.Anchored = true
		end
	end

	-- Place it on the ground 40 studs in front of the world center
	result:PivotTo(CFrame.new(0, result:GetExtentsSize().Y / 2, -40))
	result.Parent = Workspace
else
	warn("Generation failed:", result)
end
explain: We describe the car in `TextPrompt` and choose the `Car5` schema.
`pcall` runs the generation safely. If it fails, `success` is false and `result` holds the error message.
We measure the model and scale it so its longest side is 16 studs.
We anchor all parts because this is just a display model with no driving script yet.
`PivotTo` sets its position so it sits on the ground, then we put it in Workspace.

watchOut: Always wrap `GenerateModelAsync` in `pcall`. Without it, a rejected prompt or timeout crashes your script.
Generated pieces are separate parts. Without anchoring or a behavior script, they can fall apart.
Only `Car5` and `Body1` are built-in schemas. Do not expect other names to work.
Generated models can be any size, so scale them before placing them.
